metadata.headline: How does JD.com turn logistics from a retail cost into a marketplace service?

platform_lesson.title: Internal infrastructure can become ecosystem infrastructure
platform_lesson.text: JD built logistics to support its first-party retail model, where controlling warehousing and last-mile delivery helped create the speed and authenticity customers associated with JD. The same infrastructure was later opened to third-party merchants, and in 2026 JD Logistics explicitly shifted parts of its on-demand delivery business to serve third-party merchants on JD's platform directly. In the marketplace, logistics is therefore no longer only an internal Owner activity: it becomes a complementary service that Providers can consume. The platform lesson is that a capability built for a pipeline business can become ecosystem infrastructure when it is exposed as a service to other participants.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Product Listing is the Core Value Unit in the third-party marketplace boundary: a Merchant's product offer made discoverable and purchasable through JD's retail interface. JD's broader store also contains first-party inventory, but that inventory is outside the Provider side of this PBMC.

metrics.note: High-end home-appliance product pages on JD.com generated more than 100 million visits during the 2025 11.11 promotion. This is an engagement proxy for product-listing scale and attention, not a count of all live listings.

actor.explanation: Shoppers are the demand side of JD's retail platform. They can buy products sold directly by JD or by third-party Merchants; this case isolates their interaction with Marketplace supply.

metrics.note: JD.com said its annual active customers surpassed 700 million in October 2025. This is a company-wide retail-customer metric, not a third-party-marketplace-only Buyer count.

job.explanation: Shoppers want a broad selection of products with reliable quality, price, delivery and after-sales service.

gain.explanation: JD combines marketplace assortment with a retail brand strongly associated with authenticity, fulfillment speed and service.

pain.explanation: Third-party supply can create uncertainty around Merchant quality, product authenticity, service consistency and fulfillment.

transaction.explanation: Shoppers choose a third-party Merchant's listing and complete the order and payment through JD's commerce flow.

filter.explanation: Purchase access depends on account, payment, geography, inventory availability and product or fraud controls.

access_channel.explanation: Shoppers primarily access JD through its retail apps and website, with additional ecosystem entry points.

activities.explanation: Shoppers search and compare, purchase, track delivery, request service or returns and provide reviews.

resources.explanation: Shoppers contribute purchasing power, delivery information, preferences, account data and review signals.

actor.explanation: Third-party Merchants sell products through JD's online marketplace. They retain the underlying inventory and can fulfill orders themselves or use logistics services provided through the JD ecosystem.

metrics.note: During JD's 2026 618 promotion, more than 3,000 Merchants participating in 618 for the first time surpassed RMB1 million in transaction volume. This is a high-performing new-Merchant cohort, not the total Merchant population.

job.explanation: Merchants want to convert product inventory and brand presence into sales by reaching JD's large customer base.

gain.explanation: Merchants gain customer traffic plus access to marketing tools and optional integrated logistics and fulfillment services.

pain.explanation: Merchants face commissions, marketing costs, competition for traffic, strict quality requirements and service-performance expectations.

transaction.explanation: Merchants create product listings and commercial terms and then supply the purchased item, using self-fulfillment or JD-linked logistics.

filter.explanation: JD applies Merchant qualification, product, brand-authorization, quality and marketplace-conduct requirements.

access_channel.explanation: Merchants use JD's seller systems, dashboards, marketing tools and supported integrations to operate on the marketplace.

activities.explanation: Merchants manage product data, inventory, pricing, marketing, orders, customer service, fulfillment and returns.

resources.explanation: Merchants contribute products, inventory, product information, pricing, brand authorization and fulfillment capability.

actor.explanation: JD Logistics is modeled as the complementary Partner layer rather than being hidden inside the Owner. It is a separately reported and separately listed JD group company that provides warehousing, distribution, express, freight and on-demand delivery services both to JD Retail and directly to third-party Merchants.

metrics.note: JD Logistics reported 79,314 external integrated supply chain customers for the first half of 2026. Its external-customer revenue explicitly includes third-party Merchants on JD Group's marketplace, but the 79,314 figure also includes external customers outside JD.com.

job.explanation: JD Logistics turns inventory into reliable warehousing, delivery and return execution for JD Retail and Merchant customers.

gain.explanation: Marketplace and external-Merchant demand creates logistics volume, customer relationships and service revenue.

pain.explanation: The logistics layer must balance speed, service consistency, network utilization and cost across large and volatile order volumes.

transaction.explanation: JD Logistics provides logistics and supply-chain services and receives service revenue from JD Group and external customers, including marketplace Merchants.

filter.explanation: Logistics participation depends on service scope, operational requirements, product characteristics, network coverage and commercial terms.

access_channel.explanation: Merchants and JD businesses connect into warehousing, order, delivery and return services through JD Logistics systems and operating network.

activities.explanation: JD Logistics warehouses inventory, processes fulfillment, transports parcels, performs last-mile delivery and supports returns.

resources.explanation: Its logistics network, warehouses, couriers, automation, routing technology, data and supply-chain expertise are core resources.

actor.explanation: JD Retail is the operating Owner of the marketplace inside JD.com. JD.com reports JD Retail as the segment that mainly engages in online retail, online marketplace and marketing services in China.

metrics.note: JD.com reported RMB30.860 billion of marketplace and marketing revenues in Q2 2026. This is the consolidated marketplace-and-marketing revenue category supporting the marketplace layer, not a pure marketplace commission figure.

job.explanation: JD Retail must combine first-party retail and third-party Marketplace supply while preserving a consistent customer experience.

gain.explanation: Third-party Merchants broaden selection and generate marketplace, marketing and adjacent service revenue without JD owning every item.

pain.explanation: JD must coordinate two supply models, Merchant quality, ranking, pricing, fulfillment choices and customer expectations within one retail interface.

transaction.explanation: JD Retail organizes discovery, ordering, payment, Merchant economics and the handoff into the selected fulfillment route.

governance.explanation: JD governs Merchant eligibility, brand authorization, product quality, reviews, customer protections and marketplace conduct.

promotion_channel.explanation: JD attracts demand through search, recommendations, major shopping festivals, loyalty, advertising, livestreaming and its retail brand.

activities.explanation: JD Retail operates discovery, seller onboarding, marketplace rules, marketing services, checkout, customer support and transaction coordination.

resources.explanation: JD's customer base, retail brand, catalog, transaction data, marketplace technology and links to its supply-chain infrastructure are strategic resources.

current.explanation: Shoppers send the marketplace order and payment through JD Retail's commerce flow.
JD Retail provides product discovery, checkout, reviews, marketplace governance and customer-service protections.
Third-party Merchants provide product listings and pay commission or purchase applicable marketing and marketplace services.
JD Retail exposes Merchant listings to customer demand and coordinates proceeds from completed marketplace orders.
Purchases, messages and reviews create demand and reputation signals directly relevant to the Merchant.
The third-party Merchant is the economic Seller and supplies the purchased product, regardless of whether fulfillment is self-operated or delegated.
When JD Logistics is selected, it provides the physical delivery and can support reverse-logistics services for the Shopper.
Merchants can place inventory into JD Logistics' service flow and purchase warehousing, delivery or related supply-chain services.
JD Logistics returns warehousing, order fulfillment, delivery and return capabilities directly to third-party Merchants.
JD Retail supplies order volume and internal logistics demand to JD Logistics; JD reports inter-segment logistics-service transactions between the businesses.
JD Logistics provides supply-chain execution and logistics status back into JD Retail's customer and order experience.

metrics.note: Q2 2026 marketplace and marketing revenues; not pure marketplace commission revenue.
JD.com annual active customers surpassed 700M in October 2025; not Marketplace-only.
First-time 618 Merchants exceeding RMB1M transaction volume during the 2026 promotion; not total Merchants.
JD Logistics external integrated supply chain customers in H1 2026; includes JD Marketplace Merchants and customers outside JD.com.
High-end appliance product-page visits during 2025 11.11; engagement proxy, not total listing count.

sources.title: Cases only.pptx — JD.com source case
sources.note: User-supplied source reconstruction: JD.com as platform owner, shoppers as Consumers, third-party Sellers as Providers, logistics/payment/technology actors as Partners, and Product Listing as the original CVU.

sources.title: JD.com Announces Second Quarter and Interim 2026 Results
sources.note: Primary source for RMB30.860B Q2 2026 marketplace and marketing revenue, current JD Retail/JD Logistics segment boundaries, and the explicit 2026 shift of JD Logistics on-demand delivery to directly serve third-party Merchants on JD's platform.

sources.title: JD.com 2025 Form 20-F
sources.note: Primary regulatory source for the hybrid retail/marketplace architecture: third-party Merchants sell on JD Platform and can fulfill orders themselves or through JD Group logistics; JD earns commissions and provides marketing and logistics services.

sources.title: JD Logistics — Results for the Three and Six Months Ended June 30, 2026
sources.note: Regulatory-results reproduction for 79,314 external integrated supply chain customers in H1 2026 and RMB85.4B external-customer revenue. The filing states external customers include third-party Merchants on JD Group's online marketplace.

sources.title: JD.com 618 Grand Promotion Sets New Record for Shoppers
sources.note: Primary current source for the Provider-scale proxy: more than 3,000 Merchants participating in 618 for the first time surpassed RMB1M in transaction volume in 2026.

sources.title: JD.com Announces Third Quarter 2025 Results
sources.note: Primary source for the milestone of more than 700M annual active customers in October 2025.

sources.title: JD.com Strengthens Its Position as Gateway for Premium International Home Appliance Brands in China
sources.note: Primary source for the CVU engagement proxy: high-end appliance product pages generated over 100M visits during 2025 11.11.
